scale.source: Dutch uses the long scale: CLDR RBNF nl (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, nl.xml), %spellout-numbering: "1000000000: ←← miljard", "1000000000000: ←← biljoen", "1000000000000000: ←← biljard"

decimal_mark.source: CLDR number symbols for Dutch (Babel 2.18.0): decimal ',', group '.'

space_groups.source: CLDR number symbols for Dutch (Babel 2.18.0): decimal ',', group '.'; a space between digit strings separates two numbers.

compound_words.source: Dutch writes a number below a million as one word: see the RBNF rules quoted on each entry.

plural_scale_needs_count.source: "miljoenen" alone names no number; a count takes the singular: CLDR RBNF nl (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, nl.xml), %spellout-numbering: "1000000: ←← miljoen[ →→]" ("twee miljoen")

scale_noun_agrees.source: CLDR RBNF nl (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, nl.xml), %spellout-numbering: "1000000: ←← miljoen[ →→]": "twee miljoen" takes the singular

joiner_tens_units.source: Dutch puts the unit before the ten: CLDR RBNF nl (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, nl.xml), %spellout-numbering: "20: [→%%number-en→]twintig"

joiner_after_hundred.source: CLDR RBNF nl (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, nl.xml), %spellout-numbering: "100: honderd[→→]"

joiner_between_groups.source: CLDR RBNF nl (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, nl.xml), %spellout-numbering: "1000: duizend[→→]", "1000000: ←← miljoen[ →→]"

one_before_ordinal_scale_is_fraction.source: "een honderdste" is 1/100: Dutch writes a fraction with the ordinal word (Wiktionary, "honderdste")

decimal_marker.source: CLDR RBNF nl (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, nl.xml), %spellout-numbering: "x.x: ←← komma →→"

minus.source: CLDR RBNF nl (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, nl.xml), %spellout-numbering: "-x: min →→"; "minus" is the same sign word (Van Dale, "minus")

minus_idioms.source: "min of meer" puts no number after "min".

article_one.source: "een" is the indefinite article and the numeral 1; "één" with accents is only the numeral (Taalunie, Woordenlijst, "één")

of.source: Dutch has no such word in its numbers.
